name: requires data/usage dependency for setVisibility vs counts control‑flow reachability as dependency
side_a: Credit answers that distinguish the null‑guard (control flow) from actual dependency of the setVisibility logic, i.e., they say the visibility line itself does not depend on drawer even though an early return guards it.
side_b: Deduct answers that claim the end code 'depends on drawer' solely because an early return on drawer==null gates reachability, conflating control flow with dependency.

name: scopes “code at the end” to the final visibility line vs treats the whole post‑guard block (incl. drawer calls) as “the end”
side_a: Credit answers that interpret “the code at the end” as the final actionBarSubTitle.setVisibility statement and assess that line’s dependency in isolation.
side_b: Deduct answers that interpret “the end” as the broader post‑guard region and argue dependency based on the drawer‑selection calls in that block.

name: accurate control‑flow gating vs claims it 'ensures non‑null'
side_a: Credit if the answer correctly characterizes the dependency as control-flow gating (e.g., early return prevents later code) or explicitly notes no direct dependency.
side_b: Deduct if the answer incorrectly claims the early return 'ensures' the object is non-null, conflating gating with guaranteeing non-null.

name: Recognizes in-method guard/control-flow dependency vs claims external precondition/no direct dependency
side_a: no_deduct: Credit answers that explicitly tie the dependency to the method’s own null check/early return, i.e., that the subsequent code only executes when drawer is non-null because the method returns early if it is null.
side_b: deduct: Withhold credit when the answer denies a dependency or shifts it to an external assumption/precondition (e.g., says it does not directly depend on drawer being non-null or that drawer is assumed/initialized before the call), instead of acknowledging the in-method guard.
